examples.en: Many twigs broke in the wind last night.

examples.ko: 나무의 잔가지를 쳐 주면 더 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you trim a tree's twigs, it grows better.
At the campsite I made kindling out of dry twigs.
A sparrow perched on a twig is chirping.

examples.ko: 큰 줄기만 남기고 잔가지는 다 잘라 냈어요.
examples.en: I cut off all the twigs and left only the main trunk.
Please clear away the twigs that fell on the road too.

explain: 굵은 줄기나 큰 가지에서 갈라져 나온 가늘고 작은 가지를 말해요. 이야기를 할 때 핵심이 아닌 부분은 '곁가지'라고 비유해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I picked up twigs in the woods to make a fire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅에 떨어진 작은 나뭇가지를 모을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for gathering small branches that fell on the ground.

phrases.example: 이 나무는 잔가지가 많아서 빽빽해 보여요.
phrases.en: This tree has many twigs, so it looks dense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무 모양을 설명할 때 '많다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 많다 to describe how a tree looks.

phrases.example: 이야기의 곁가지는 빼고 중요한 것만 말해요.
phrases.en: Leave out the side details of the story and say only what matters.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기에서 핵심이 아닌 부분을 비유해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for the non-essential parts of a story.

explain_en: It refers to the thin, small branches that split off from a thick trunk or big branch. When talking about a story, the non-essential parts are sometimes called '곁가지' as a metaphor.

examples.ko: 이 호텔은 바다 조망이 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This hotel has a really good sea view.
I chose this apartment because I was drawn to the view.

examples.ko: 산 정상에서 도시 전체의 조망을 즐겼어요.
examples.en: I enjoyed the view of the whole city from the summit.
The view isn't great because the building in front blocks it.
A dispute arose among neighbors over the right to a view.

examples.ko: 전망대에서 본 조망 덕분에 피곤이 싹 풀렸어요.
examples.en: The view from the observatory made my tiredness disappear.

explain: 높은 곳에서 멀리까지 내다보이는 경치를 말해요. '전망'과 비슷하지만 '전망'은 앞날의 예측이라는 뜻도 있어서, 풍경만 가리킬 때 '조망'이 더 분명해요. 부동산이나 숙소 소개에서 '조망이 좋다', '조망권'으로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 이 방은 산이 보여서 조망이 좋아요.
phrases.en: This room has a good view because you can see the mountains.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경치가 잘 보인다는 뜻으로 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for having a nice scenic view.

phrases.example: 앞에 건물이 생기면 조망권을 잃을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If a building goes up in front, we could lose our right to a view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 경치를 볼 수 있는 권리를 뜻하고 집 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The right to enjoy a good view, used in talk about housing.

phrases.en: I reserved a room with an ocean view.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 보이는지를 앞에 붙여 숙소 소개에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put what you see in front; common in lodging descriptions.

explain_en: Written/formal; looking out over a wide scene (창밖 조망) It means the scenery you can see far away from a high place. It is similar to '전망', but '전망' can also mean a forecast of the future, so '조망' is clearer when you mean only the scenery. It is common in real estate and lodging descriptions as '조망이 좋다' or '조망권'.

t90.ax: This hotel has a really good sea view.

examples.en: I saw a sea horse for the first time at the aquarium.
The sea horse is holding onto seaweed with its tail.

examples.ko: 아이가 해마 모양 인형을 갖고 싶어 했어요.
examples.en: The child wanted a sea horse-shaped doll.
My friend said the sea horse looks like a horse.
I want to swim with sea horses in the ocean.

examples.ko: 해마의 수컷이 새끼를 낳는다는 사실을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned that the male sea horse gives birth to the young.

explain: 뇌에서 기억을 맡는 부분도 '해마'라고 불러서 같은 소리의 말이에요. 문장 속 내용을 보면 동물인지 뇌인지 알 수 있어요. 동물 해마는 머리 모양이 말을 닮아서 이름에 '마'(말)가 들어가요.

phrases.en: I saw one sea horse at the aquarium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이라서 '마리'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is an animal, so it is counted with 마리.

phrases.en: The sea horse swims slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바다 동물 해마의 움직임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes how the sea animal moves.

phrases.en: The hippocampus in the brain handles memory.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뇌의'가 붙으면 동물이 아니라 뇌의 부분이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 뇌의, it means the brain part, not the animal.

explain_en: The part of the brain that handles memory is also called 해마, so the same word has two meanings. The context tells you whether it is the animal or the brain. The animal has 마, meaning horse, in its name because its head looks like a horse.

examples.ko: 방에 들어가자 후끈 더운 공기가 느껴졌어요.
examples.en: When I entered the room, I felt a wave of hot air.
I was embarrassed and my face flushed hot.
I turned on the heater and the room warmed up quickly.

examples.ko: 매운 음식을 먹었더니 온몸이 후끈 더워졌어요.
examples.en: After eating spicy food, my whole body got hot.

examples.ko: 열차 문이 열리자 후끈 열기가 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: When the train door opened, a rush of heat came in.
I was so embarrassed that even my ears burned.

explain: '후끈 달아오르다', '후끈 더워지다'처럼 갑자기 열기가 확 느껴질 때 써요. 부끄러움이나 화로 얼굴이 뜨거워질 때도 쓰고, 분위기가 뜨거울 때 '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'라고도 해요. 약하게 따뜻한 건 '따끈'이 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: I was embarrassed and my face flushed hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼굴이나 분위기가 갑자기 뜨거워질 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a face or mood suddenly heating up.

phrases.en: When I opened the door, the room suddenly got hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열기가 갑자기 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when heat is suddenly felt.

phrases.en: It's very hot inside the sauna.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여 상태를 말하는 형용사로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -하다 it works as an adjective describing a state.

explain_en: Warmth filling a space or air, like a heated room (방 안이 후끈) It is used when heat suddenly hits you, as in '후끈 달아오르다' and '후끈 더워지다'. It also fits a face heating up from embarrassment or anger, and a heated mood, '분위기가 후끈 달아오르다'. For gentle warmth, '따끈' fits better.

en: to be happy; to be joyous; to be auspicious

examples.en: Today is a joyous day for our family.
A baby was born, so the whole house is celebrating.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 모여 경사스럽게 잔치를 열었어요.
examples.en: The neighbors gathered and held a festive party.
The news of the acceptance made the whole family joyful.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 결혼하면 정말 경사스러울 거예요.
examples.en: It will be truly a happy occasion if the two get married.

examples.ko: 이렇게 경사스러워서 오늘은 제가 밥을 살게요.
examples.en: It's such a happy occasion that I'll buy dinner today.

explain: '경사'는 결혼, 합격, 출산 같은 좋은 일을 말해서 '경사스럽다'도 집안이나 동네의 큰 기쁨에 써요. 일상에서는 '좋은 일', '기쁜 일'을 더 많이 쓰고 '경사스럽다'는 조금 격식 있게 들려요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '경사스러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: I heard some joyous news from a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경사스럽다'를 명사 앞에 쓰면 결혼이나 출산 같은 기쁜 일을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun, it describes happy events like a wedding or a birth.

phrases.en: A grandchild was born, so the whole family is full of joy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 집안이나 날의 큰 기쁨을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, used to describe the great joy of a family or a day.

phrases.en: You passed? What great news!
phrases.nuance_ko: '경사스럽다'보다 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a more casual, spoken way to say something happy has happened.

explain_en: Formal: a happy occasion like a wedding or birth (경사스러운 날). 경사 refers to happy family events such as weddings, passing an exam, or a birth, so 경사스럽다 describes a big joy shared by a family or town. In daily talk people say 좋은 일 or 기쁜 일 more often; 경사스럽다 sounds a bit formal. It is ㅂ-irregular, giving 경사스러워요.

dis.h: auspicious; a joyful occasion or event

p.n: 행복하다 is personal happiness; 경사스럽다 marks a celebratory, auspicious occasion.

t90.ax: Today is a joyous day for our family.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 연인에 대한 독점욕이 너무 강해요.
examples.en: He is too possessive of his partner.
The child shows possessiveness over the new toy.
Possessiveness made the friendship difficult.
Love and possessiveness are different.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 독점욕이 강해서 제 무릎을 안 비켜 줘요.
examples.en: My puppy is so possessive that he won't give up my lap.
Excessive possessiveness wears the other person out.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음이에요. 연인·친구 관계에서 쓰면 '집착', '질투'와 가까운 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '독점욕이 강하다', '독점욕을 보이다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My friend is struggling because of possessiveness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 쓰며 보통 부정적인 결과와 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give a reason, usually leading to a negative result.

phrases.example: 동생이 생기자 형은 엄마에 대한 독점욕을 느꼈어요.
phrases.en: When a sibling was born, the older brother felt possessive of his mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 마음이 생겼다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that such a feeling arose.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 독점욕이 강해서 저를 다른 친구들과 못 만나게 해요.
phrases.en: My friend is very possessive, so he doesn't let me meet my other friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격이나 태도를 말할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for describing someone's personality or attitude.

explain_en: It is the wish to keep a person or thing all to yourself. Used about partners or friends, it feels negative, close to obsession or jealousy. Common patterns are '독점욕이 강하다' and '독점욕을 보이다'.

en: to be hindered; to be disturbed; to get in the way

examples.en: Loud noise gets in the way of studying.
I'm sorry if I was in the way.
I'll go in quietly so I won't disturb anyone.
Please move the things that are in the way.

examples.ko: 이어폰 소리가 옆 사람에게 방해될까 봐 줄였어요.
examples.en: I turned down my earphones in case they bothered the person next to me.
Tell me if it bothers you.

explain: 어떤 일에 걸림돌이 될 때 써요. '방해가 되다'라고도 해요. 정중하게 '방해되지 않을까요?'라고 물을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The music gets in the way of my sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '방해되다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 조금 더 자연스럽게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 방해되다 and sounds a bit more natural in speech.

phrases.en: Quiet sounds don't get in the way of studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괜찮다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say something is not a problem.
phrases.en_equiv: it doesn't get in the way

phrases.en: Wouldn't it be a bother if I call now?
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심스럽게 물어볼 때 쓰는 정중한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask carefully whether you might be disturbing someone.

explain_en: Use it when something gets in the way of an activity. You can also say '방해가 되다'. A polite way to ask is '방해되지 않을까요?'.

en: to surge; to well up; to spring up

examples.ko: 아침 운동을 하면 힘이 샘솟는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: When I exercise in the morning, I feel energy welling up.
Starting a new job makes my motivation surge.

examples.ko: 아이를 보면 사랑이 샘솟아서 저도 모르게 웃어요.
examples.en: When I see my child, love wells up and I smile without realizing it.
Water started to well up from under the rock.

examples.ko: 좋은 노래를 들으면 아이디어가 샘솟곤 해요.
examples.en: Ideas often pour out when I listen to a good song.
Receiving support made my courage surge.

explain: 샘에서 물이 계속 나오듯이, 힘·용기·의욕·아이디어처럼 마음속에서 계속 생겨날 때 많이 써요. 보통 '힘이 샘솟다'처럼 '이/가'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I feel energy welling up after eating a good meal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸과 마음에 힘이 계속 생길 때 가장 많이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when energy keeps rising within you.

phrases.en: Good ideas keep coming when I take a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 계속 떠오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ideas keep coming one after another.

phrases.example: 친구의 응원 덕분에 샘솟는 용기를 느꼈어요.
phrases.en: Thanks to my friend's support, I felt courage welling up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '샘솟는' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form '샘솟는' describes a noun that keeps arising.

explain_en: Water, energy or hope springing up; positive. Like water keeps flowing from a spring, it is often used for things that keep arising inside you, such as strength, courage, motivation and ideas. It is usually used with '이/가', as in '힘이 샘솟다'.

t90.ax: Receiving support made my courage surge.

examples.ko: 이 냄새를 맡으면 어린 시절을 연상해요.
examples.en: This smell makes me think of my childhood.
What do you associate with the color red?
I thought of the sea from that name.
I tried a word-association game.

examples.ko: 여름 하면 수박을 연상하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people think of watermelon when they think of summer.
I linked the two incidents in my mind and became anxious.

explain: '생각하다'는 일부러 하는 것이고, '연상하다'는 어떤 것을 보거나 듣다가 다른 것이 저절로 떠오를 때 써요. 보통 '~에서 ~을/를 연상하다'로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '떠올리다'가 더 자연스럽고, 어떤 것이 다른 것을 떠오르게 하면 '연상시키다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 노래를 들으면 옛 친구를 떠올려요.
phrases.en: When I hear this song, I think of an old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연상하다'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural word than '연상하다' in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: This picture reminds me of spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 다른 것을 생각나게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that something makes you think of something else.

phrases.example: 이 향기를 맡으면 바다가 연상이 돼요.
phrases.en: When I smell this scent, the sea comes to mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 저절로 떠오르는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a thought comes to mind on its own.

explain_en: The person actively thinks of B from A (눈을 보면 방학을 연상하다) '생각하다' is thinking on purpose, while 연상하다 is used when seeing or hearing one thing makes another thing come to mind by itself. It is usually said as '~에서 ~을/를 연상하다'. In daily talk '떠올리다' is more natural, and when something makes you think of another thing, you say '연상시키다'.

en: to be dispirited; to be dejected; to be despondent

examples.en: The exam I prepared for so long was canceled, and I feel deflated.

examples.ko: 결과를 확인하고 나니 몸에서 힘이 빠지고 허탈했어요.
examples.en: After checking the result, my strength drained away and I felt empty.
When you feel drained like that, you don't want to do anything, right?

examples.ko: 열심히 모은 돈을 한순간에 잃고 나서 허탈하다고 했어요.
examples.en: After losing the money he saved up in an instant, he said he felt hollow.

examples.ko: 큰 행사가 끝나면 허탈해서 며칠 동안 멍하게 지내요.
examples.en: After a big event ends, I feel let down and spend a few days in a daze.

examples.ko: 그의 허탈한 웃음을 보니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Seeing his hollow smile made my heart ache.

explain: 기대했던 일이 끝나거나 헛수고가 됐을 때 몸과 마음의 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이에요. '허무하다'는 모든 게 덧없다는 생각에 가깝고, '허탈하다'는 맥이 풀린 상태에 가까워요. 같은 느낌을 '맥이 빠지다'라고도 하고, 명사로는 '허탈감'을 써요.

phrases.en: He sat there with a dejected look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 빠진 얼굴을 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form for a face drained of energy.

phrases.en: Everyone felt dejected after seeing the result.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 허탈함을 느끼는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe other people showing dejection.

phrases.en: I prepared hard but it was canceled, so I lost heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허탈하다와 비슷하게 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses a similar drained feeling to 허탈하다.

explain_en: It is the feeling of strength draining from body and mind when something you looked forward to ends or turns out to be wasted effort. '허무하다' is closer to the thought that everything is futile, while '허탈하다' is closer to being left limp and deflated. People also say '맥이 빠지다' for the same feeling, and the noun is '허탈감'.

en: to go crazy; to go mad; to be out of one's mind

examples.en: The traffic is so bad that I am losing my mind.
My younger sibling goes crazy for games.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에 휴대폰이 고장 나서 환장할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: My phone broke the day before the exam, and I nearly lost it.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 나오면 팬들이 환장하며 소리를 질러요.
examples.en: When that singer appears, the fans go wild and scream.
I have a friend who is crazy about spicy food.

examples.ko: 일이 계속 꼬여서 환장하는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Things kept going wrong, and I thought I would go insane.

explain: 환장하다는 너무 화가 나거나 좋아서 정신이 없을 때 써요. 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 거친 말이라서 어른이나 공식 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. '환장할 노릇이다'는 어찌할 바를 모르게 답답하다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I have so much homework, I'm going crazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 힘들거나 답답할 때 친한 사이에서 쓰는 거친 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A rough expression among friends for being overwhelmed or frustrated.

phrases.example: 약속 시간이 다 됐는데 열쇠가 없어서 환장할 노릇이에요.
phrases.en: It's time for my appointment but I can't find my key. It's maddening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어찌할 바를 몰라 답답한 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a situation so frustrating you don't know what to do.

phrases.en: My friend goes crazy for fried chicken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 너무 좋아할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you love something to the extreme.

explain_en: 환장하다 says you are so angry or so thrilled that you can't think straight. It is rough, casual speech between friends, so avoid it with elders or in formal situations. 환장할 노릇이다 is a common phrase for a situation that is maddening and leaves you helpless.

examples.en: There's a stink coming from the shoe cabinet.
The stink from the drain made me open the window.
I sprayed air freshener to get rid of the stink.
The old cheese gave off a terrible stink.
I don't know where the stink is coming from.
The sweaty socks gave off a stink.

explain: 똥이나 썩은 것, 오래된 신발과 양말처럼 코를 찌르는 안 좋은 냄새예요. '고린내'는 비슷하지만 느낌이 조금 작은 말이에요. '냄새가 나다'보다 더 불쾌한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Something about this contract smells fishy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 괜찮아 보여도 뭔가 수상하고 떳떳하지 못한 느낌이 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used when something seems suspicious or shady even though it looks fine on the surface.

explain_en: Foul smell — rotten, dung-like or dirty odor, widely used (신발장에서 이상한 구린내가 나서 창문을 열었어요.) This is a nasty smell like feces, rotten things, or old shoes and socks. '고린내' is a similar word with a slightly smaller feel. It feels more unpleasant than just '냄새가 나다'.

examples.en: Don't say things like that.
There's no need to get mad over something like that.
I don't want to hear an excuse like that.
Why did you buy something like that?
Don't believe a rumor like that.
Stop thinking that kind of thought.

explain: '그런'과 비슷하지만 말하는 사람이 그것을 하찮게 보거나 못마땅해하는 느낌이 들어요. 그래서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 비슷한 말로 '이딴', '저딴'이 있고, 가까운 사이에서 화나거나 가볍게 말할 때 나와요.

phrases.en: Please stop saying such nonsense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말을 하찮게 여기거나 못마땅해할 때 쓰는 말이라 가까운 사이에서만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dismissive of what someone said; only for close relationships.

phrases.en: You shouldn't talk in that way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 말투나 행동이 마음에 안 들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you dislike someone's tone or behavior.

phrases.en: I want to stop doing this kind of work now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 것을 하찮게 볼 때 쓰는 말로, '그딴'과 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The version for something near the speaker, paired with 그딴.

explain_en: Like 그런, but it sounds dismissive or disapproving, so don't use it with elders or people you just met. 이딴 and 저딴 are the same pattern, and you hear them among close friends when someone is annoyed or casual.

examples.ko: 까짓 시험 한 번 망쳤다고 포기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give up just because you blew one little test.
Ah, what the heck, let's give it a try.

examples.ko: 까짓 돈 몇 푼 때문에 싸우지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't fight over a measly bit of money.
Anyone makes a trifling mistake like that.

examples.ko: 까짓것 안 되면 다시 하면 돼요.
examples.en: So what if it doesn't work? You can just do it again.
So what if we get a little wet in the rain?

explain: 별것 아니라고 낮춰 말하거나 큰 결심을 가볍게 말할 때 써요. 뒤에는 '것, 거, 일, 돈'처럼 명사가 오고, '그까짓'은 더 강하게 말하는 형태예요. 친한 사이의 말투라서 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: Don't cry over such a trivial thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '까짓'보다 더 강하게 낮춰 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A stronger form of 까짓, belittling something more strongly.

phrases.en: Oh, what the heck, let's give it a try.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 결심을 가볍게 말할 때 쓰는 친한 사이의 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual phrase used among friends to take a big decision lightly.

phrases.example: 까짓 돈 얼마 안 돼요. 신경 쓰지 마세요.
phrases.en: It's only a little money. Don't worry about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 별것 아니라고 말할 때 쓰고, 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to play down money; better not to use it with someone older.

explain_en: It is used to belittle something as trivial or to casually shrug off a big decision. A noun follows it, such as '것', '거', '일' or '돈', and '그까짓' is a stronger form. It is casual talk, so avoid it with seniors.
